title: Exterior basis of quotient-coefficient Koszul homology
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I=(f)$ an ideal generated by a tuple $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$, $n$ a natural number, and $b$ a basis of $I/I^2$ over $B=A/I$ indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(r)$ [def-sc-koszul-conormal-comparison]. Write $L=K_A(f)\otimes_A B$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. There is an $A$-module isomorphism $e:\bigwedge_B^n(I/I^2)\cong H_n(L)$ such that for every $n$-element subset $s$ of $\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, with its increasing enumeration $j_1,\ldots,j_n$, there is a cycle $z_s$ whose inclusion in $L_n$ is $(e_{j_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{j_n})\otimes1$ and whose homology class is $e(b_{j_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge b_{j_n})$. Regularity of $f$ and normalization of $b$ are not assumed. Empty sequences, empty exterior bases and the zero quotient ring are included.

source.place: dpa.tex, lemma-divided-powers-on-tor, free-resolution tensor computation; Tags 0623 and 062I for the Koszul differential and conormal basis

proof.text: Reuse the existing private standard-wedge contraction formula from KoszulBaseChangeIso via proof-only import all. It is a sum of smaller wedges with coefficients signed generators f_i. After tensoring with A/I each coefficient acts by zero. Exterior basis expansion and the tensor universal property therefore prove that every differential of L is zero.

The representation map of the exterior basis induced by b identifies the source with finitely supported coefficient vectors over A/I. TensorProduct.equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft identifies the tensor term with the same coefficient vectors using the standard exterior basis over A. Compose the first representation map, restricted to A, with the inverse of the second.

Since incoming and outgoing differentials are zero, HomologicalComplex.iCyclesIso and isoHomologyπ give the cycle and homology isomorphisms. Compose with the term isomorphism; apply the inverse cycle inclusion to each term basis vector. The isomorphism inverse identity gives the specified cycle inclusion, and the composite definition gives its homology class.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_koszul_quotient_tensor_homology_basis
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (n r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I)
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (A ⧸ I) I.Cotangent) :
    let K := ExteriorAlgebra.koszulComplex A r f
    let T := (tensorRight (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)
    ∃ e : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj
        (ModuleCat.of (A ⧸ I) (⋀[A ⧸ I]^n I.Cotangent)) ≅ (T.obj K).homology n,
      ∀ s : Set.powersetCard (Fin r) n,
        ∃ z : (T.obj K).cycles n,
          (T.obj K).iCycles n z =
            (exteriorPower.ιMulti A n
              (fun j ↦ Finsupp.single (Set.powersetCard.ofFinEmbEquiv.symm s j) 1))
                ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : A ⧸ I) ∧
          e.hom (b.exteriorPower n s) = (T.obj K).homologyπ n z
